25	| **v1 baseline** | `v1.0.0` tagged 2026-07-04 — 187/189 roadmap tasks (~99%); all 8 weekly exit gates met; deployed to Azure Container Apps; retro at [retro-v1.md](retro-v1.md); full ledger at [progress-v1.md](progress-v1.md) |
26	| **Current cycle** | **v1.1 — 6 weeks + a stretch week, 2026-07-04 → 2026-08-15 (+ W7 stretch to 2026-08-22)** (planned 2026-07-04 from [context/post-v1-roadmap.md](../context/post-v1-roadmap.md)). Sequencing is **subscription-driven**: Weeks 1–3 extract everything that needs the expiring Snowflake (lapses within days) and Azure (~2026-07-25) subscriptions, then wind down gracefully; Weeks 4–6 run the roadmap's recommended opening sequence (Theme-1 `schema_drift` + `anomaly` → scale-aware execution G-b → incident/lineage design G-d — the G-d design half, #596, was pulled forward and done in W3, 2026-07-10) on cloud-independent infra; W7 is the stretch/burn-down buffer. See [Cycle plan](#cycle-plan--v11-6-weeks--stretch-2026-07-04--2026-08-22) below. |
27	| **Open issues** | **30** open repo-wide / **26** in the **`v1.1 Backlog`** milestone, re-counted with `gh issue list` on 2026-08-09 after PRs [#1263](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1263) (closes [#1228](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1228)), [#1265](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1265) (closes [#1221](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1221)), [#1268](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1268) (closes [#1253](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1253)), [#1269](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1269) (closes [#1230](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1230)), and [#1271](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1271) (closes [#1251](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1251)) all merged — five closes offset by filing [#1266](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1266) (the #1221 review's deferred driver-guard finding — `connect_args`'s psycopg2-specific keys have no driver-family guard, a pre-existing gap #1221 amplified rather than introduced) and [#1270](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1270) (the #1251 review's repo-wide SecretStore-fake sweep follow-up — corrected from an initial 10-file scope to ~31 files after a second review pass found the first undercounted by roughly 2x). **#1228** (merged earlier this session, its docs recount deferred to this batch — the two remaining lineage abort-instead-of-descend sites in the Snowflake pull, `_from_access_history`'s bare `raise` and a floor-failure-after-successful-traversal path, now skip just the affected tier and return the traversal's own edges as a degraded non-prunable result instead of discarding real observed lineage). **#1221** (DB pool keepalives): a warm pooled connection surviving a silent network partition could hang a read forever — `pool_pre_ping`'s own `SELECT 1` has no OS-level floor under it. Fixed with TCP keepalives (`keepalives_idle`/`interval`/`count`) on the shared engine's `connect_args`, one layer under #1102's `connect_timeout`. Review found the migrate-job engine (`alembic/env.py`, its own independent engine, exposed to the same gap and test-enforced-parity-tracked per its own docstring) hadn't been mirrored — fixed same-PR with a matching AST regression test; the driver-guard gap was deferred to #1266 above rather than fixed inline, to keep the PR focused. **#1253** (`observed_value` retention sweep): `purge_expired_sample_failures` scrubbed `sample_failures` but never the sibling list-shaped `observed_value` JSONB — correctly redacted on every read since #1252, but persisting indefinitely with no PII-minimization sweep. Fixed with a shared `_purge_column` helper reused across both columns. **#1230** (PII classifier evidence-window, option 2 chosen): the #1196 sample cap narrowed the classifier's evidence to 20 rows at capture time for pandas-backed datasources, which can flip a genuinely-PII column to "not PII" on a noisy 20-row window. Fixed by persisting a compact per-column `value_signal_summary` (5 small ints) over the FULL pre-cap population alongside the capped rows, which the classifier prefers when present and validates before trusting (rejects a summary with an inflated/inconsistent sub-count). A `/code-review` round live-verified a real crash — `_valid_summary`'s except clause didn't catch `OverflowError`, so a persisted JSONB summary with a huge float (`"n": 1e400` → `inf`) 500'd the entire read path instead of degrading to "no summary" — and found the summary wasn't threaded into the sibling `partial_unexpected_list`'s redaction (only `unexpected_index_list`'s), leaving a column masked on one list still shown on the other for the same run; both fixed and mutation-checked same-PR. **#1251** (consolidate hand-rolled `SecretStore` test doubles): five files each hand-rolled a near-identical class implementing the `SecretStore` Protocol, folded into one shared `backend/tests/support/fake_secret_store.py::FakeSecretStore`. The migration surfaced a real bug along the way — FastAPI's dependency-override resolution introspects the override CALLABLE's own signature, so a bare class (not a lambda) with constructor params, even all-defaulted ones, gets those params bound as request-level params and corrupts body validation for the endpoint under test; a bare `_WriteFailStore()` override was making `POST /connections` 422 instead of ever reaching the route. Review found the fix was patched inline at only the two call sites that hit it rather than encoded at the seam — promoted into a shared `override_secret_store(app, store)` helper (documented in the module docstring) in a same-PR follow-up commit, and `test_admin.py`'s pre-existing `_with_store` now delegates to it instead of duplicating the same lambda wrap. (Previous — **44** open repo-wide / **27** in the **`v1.1 Backlog`** milestone, re-counted with `gh issue list` on 2026-08-09 after PR [#1260](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1260) merged, closing [#1226](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1226) — net unchanged, offset by filing [#1261](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1261). **#1226**: when every alert channel failed, `CompositePublisher._fan_out_delivered_first` logged a full traceback per failing channel and then the caller (`dispatch.py::publish_connection_health`, `main.py::_poll_staleness_loop`) logged the SAME last-channel traceback a second time via its own bare `except Exception:`. Fixed with a plain marker attribute (`mark_already_logged`/`was_already_logged` in `alerting/base.py`, the same stash-on-the-object technique already used by `celery_app.py`'s `_REQUEST_ID_RESET_ATTR`) the composite sets on the re-raised error, so both callers downgrade to a warning for an error the composite already reported, while anything the composite never saw still gets a full traceback. The analogy was wrong — `pipeline_runs` is workspace-wide orchestrator telemetry with no suite-ownership concept, whereas a near-miss is derived *wholly* from `trigger_binding` rows, which are suite-owned config the sibling `GET /trigger-bindings` already scopes. It now applies the same `accessible_suite_ids` filter, with `include_all` for a workspace admin. # DataQ — Progress tracker (post-v1)

> The **live task tracker**, active since `v1.0.0` (tagged 2026-07-04). The completed v1
> ledger — the per-PR record of the 8-week roadmap, Weeks 1–8 — is **archived, frozen at the
> tag, in [progress-v1.md](progress-v1.md)** (companion: [retro-v1.md](retro-v1.md)).
> **Updated at the end of every PR** — the PR template has a checkbox to enforce.
> Source of truth for "what's done vs. what's left" in the current cycle. CLAUDE.md §13
> carries only the headline.

## Status legend

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| ✅ | Done — PR merged to `main` |
| 🟡 | In progress — open PR or partially shipped |
| ⬜ | Not started |
| 🔵 | Deferred / scope-changed (with note) |

---

| **v1 baseline** | `v1.0.0` tagged 2026-07-04 — 187/189 roadmap tasks (~99%); all 8 weekly exit gates met; deployed to Azure Container Apps; retro at [retro-v1.md](retro-v1.md); full ledger at [progress-v1.md](progress-v1.md) |

Sequencing is **subscription-driven**: Weeks 1–3 extract everything that needs the expiring Snowflake (lapses within days) and Azure (~2026-07-25) subscriptions, then wind down gracefully; Weeks 4–6 run the roadmap's recommended opening sequence (Theme-1 `schema_drift` + `anomaly` → scale-aware execution G-b → incident/lineage design G-d — the G-d design half, #596, was pulled forward and done in W3, 2026-07-10) on cloud-independent infra; W7 is the stretch/burn-down buffer. See [Cycle plan](#cycle-plan--v11-6-weeks--stretch-2026-07-04--2026-08-22) below. |

The migration surfaced a real bug along the way — FastAPI's dependency-override resolution introspects the override CALLABLE's own signature, so a bare class (not a lambda) with constructor params, even all-defaulted ones, gets those params bound as request-level params and corrupts body validation for the endpoint under test; a bare `_WriteFailStore()` override was making `POST /connections` 422 instead of ever reaching the route. (Previous — **44** open repo-wide / **27** in the **`v1.1 Backlog`** milestone, re-counted with `gh issue list` on 2026-08-09 after PR [#1260](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1260) merged, closing [#1226](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1226) — net unchanged, offset by filing [#1261](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1261). **#1226**: when every alert channel failed, `CompositePublisher._fan_out_delivered_first` logged a full traceback per failing channel and then the caller (`dispatch.py::publish_connection_health`, `main.py::_poll_staleness_loop`) logged the SAME last-channel traceback a second time via its own bare `except Exception:`. One idea deliberately deferred rather than acted on: centralizing the downgrade in the structlog processor chain (the CLAUDE.md §10 "redact at the logger, not the call site" precedent) — reasonable for 3+ callers, premature for the 2 that exist today — filed as #1261. As written, any signed-in user could enumerate the `(provider, pipeline_or_dag_id, binding_env)` of bindings on suites they cannot see. It now applies the same `accessible_suite_ids` filter, with `include_all` for a workspace admin. Three more were honesty-of-display: the panel picked the FIRST matching near-miss with `.find()`, so a second live mismatch on the same binding — two orchestrator connections reporting one DAG id against two different wrong envs, i.e. literally the #1186 ambiguity the feature exists to catch — was hidden behind the first; a failed near-miss fetch rendered identically to "no mismatch", so an outage read as healthy on the very screen built to surface it (the ADR-0039 lesson, in a new place); and the tooltip asserted the present tense ("runs keep landing in X … this binding has not fired and won't") for anything inside the 48h window while `updated_at` was fetched, typed, threaded through and never rendered — so a binding fixed an hour ago kept being told it was still broken. Fixed with TCP keepalives (`keepalives_idle`/`interval`/`count`) on the shared engine's `connect_args`, one layer under #1102's `connect_timeout`. Review found the migrate-job engine (`alembic/env.py`, its own independent engine, exposed to the same gap and test-enforced-parity-tracked per its own docstring) hadn't been mirrored — fixed same-PR with a matching AST regression test; the driver-guard gap was deferred to #1266 above rather than fixed inline, to keep the PR focused. **#1253** (`observed_value` retention sweep): `purge_expired_sample_failures` scrubbed `sample_failures` but never the sibling list-shaped `observed_value` JSONB — correctly redacted on every read since #1252, but persisting indefinitely with no PII-minimization sweep. Fixed with a shared `_purge_column` helper reused across both columns. **#1230** (PII classifier evidence-window, option 2 chosen): the #1196 sample cap narrowed the classifier's evidence to 20 rows at capture time for pandas-backed datasources, which can flip a genuinely-PII column to "not PII" on a noisy 20-row window. Fixed by persisting a compact per-column `value_signal_summary` (5 small ints) over the FULL pre-cap population alongside the capped rows, which the classifier prefers when present and validates before trusting (rejects a summary with an inflated/inconsistent sub-count).
